subject: How to parse a character to add_tooltip() as variable?

messages.author: 697b680d95df20fd
messages.subject: How to parse a character to add_tooltip() as variable?
parts:
Hi guys,

I tried to let users to pick x and y variables for ggvis() from shiny's input_text box. The return from shiny's input_text is a character variable. For example, let's use mtcars, the input_text:

    > input_text
     [1] "mpg"  "cyl"  "disp" "hp"   "drat" "wt"   "qsec" "vs"   "am"  
    [10] "gear" "carb"

To plot ggvis(~wt, ~mpg), I can do 

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points() 

But I have no success to parse input_text to add_tooltip(). I tried

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points() %>% add_tooltip(function(df) df[[input_text[6]]])

    or

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points() %>% add_tooltip(function(df) df$wt)


In both cases, the plot was generated successfully, but add_tooltip() did not work.

Any suggestion?

Thanks a lot,

Ying
